metadata.description: Starter landing zone configuration for organizations getting started with AWS

sections.name: Basic Information
sections.description: Organization details and AWS region selection

questions.text: What is your organization's name?
questions.help_text: This will be used in account names and resource tags

questions.text: Where is your organization primarily based?
questions.help_text: Just tell me your location (city or country) - I'll figure out the best AWS region for you

inference.hint: Map user's location to the nearest AWS region that supports Control Tower. Consider: geographic proximity, data residency requirements, and service availability. Common mappings: UK/London → eu-west-2, Australia/Sydney → ap-southeast-2, US East Coast → us-east-1, US West Coast → us-west-2, Germany/Netherlands → eu-central-1, Singapore/Southeast Asia → ap-southeast-1, Japan → ap-northeast-1, Canada → ca-central-1
inference.validation_note: MUST store a valid AWS region CODE (e.g., eu-west-2, us-east-1, ap-southeast-2). Do the location->region mapping yourself and record ONLY the region code as home_region -- NEVER store the user's raw city/country/phrase. If the location is ambiguous (e.g. 'Washington' = WA state vs Washington DC), ask the user which region. A non-region value is rejected by the generator (issue #110).

questions.presentation_template: Based on your location, I recommend **{{value}}** ({{region_label}}) as your home region. This hosts your Control Tower and centralized services close to your organization for best performance.

questions.text: Tell me about your organization - roughly how many people?
questions.help_text: This helps me suggest the right level of infrastructure complexity

inference.hint: Classify organization size based on employee count: <50 people → small, 50-500 people → medium, 500+ people → large. If user gives approximate numbers like 'about 30' or 'around 100', classify accordingly. If they describe as 'startup' or 'small team' → small, 'mid-sized company' → medium, 'enterprise' or 'large corporation' → large

questions.presentation_template: Based on your {{employee_description}}, I'll classify this as **{{size_label}}**. This means we'll {{recommendation}}.

recommendations.small: keep the infrastructure simple with just essential accounts
recommendations.medium: include additional infrastructure accounts for better organization
recommendations.large: plan for full infrastructure accounts and more complex networking

questions.text: What's your team's experience with AWS?
questions.help_text: Just describe your AWS background - I'll figure out the right complexity level

inference.hint: Classify AWS experience: 'never used AWS' or 'just getting started' or 'new to cloud' → beginner. 'used EC2/S3' or 'ran some workloads' or 'familiar with basics' → intermediate. 'production workloads' or 'infrastructure as code' or 'multi-account experience' or 'AWS certified' → advanced

questions.presentation_template: Based on your experience ({{experience_description}}), I'll set this up for **{{level_label}}** users. This means {{recommendation}}.

recommendations.beginner: we'll use straightforward configurations and avoid complex automation
recommendations.intermediate: we'll include some automation while keeping things manageable
recommendations.advanced: we can use more sophisticated patterns and assume AWS familiarity

questions.text: How quickly do you need the landing zone deployed?
questions.help_text: Determines deployment approach and prioritization

questions.text: Do you need a dedicated Network account for centralized networking?
questions.help_text: Recommended for centralized network management and shared connectivity. Required if you want centralized internet egress via an Inspection/Egress VPC.

questions.text: Do you need a SharedServices account for shared resources like Active Directory or DNS?
questions.help_text: Useful for hosting shared services accessed by multiple accounts

questions.text: Do you need a Monitoring account for centralized observability tools?
questions.help_text: Recommended for centralized logging, metrics, and monitoring dashboards

questions.text: Security is set up by Control Tower. These Organizational Units will be created: Infrastructure, Workloads, Sandbox, Exceptions. Do you need any additional OUs?
questions.help_text: Enter comma-separated list of additional OU names, or leave blank

sections.name: Security and Governance
sections.description: Service control policies and governance settings

questions.text: Should accounts be prevented from leaving the organization?
questions.help_text: Strongly recommended - prevents accidental or unauthorized account removal

questions.text: Do you want to restrict which AWS regions can be used?
questions.help_text: Limits resource creation to approved regions for compliance and cost control

questions.text: Which geographic areas should be allowed?
questions.help_text: Just describe which parts of the world - I'll map to the right AWS regions. Important: these must be a subset of the regions your existing Control Tower landing zone already governs - org-wide StackSets (e.g. EBS encryption) cannot deploy to a region Control Tower does not govern. Check your governed regions in the Control Tower console (Landing zone settings) or via 'aws controltower get-landing-zone'.

inference.hint: Map geographic descriptions to AWS region code arrays. 'Europe' or 'EU' → [eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-central-1, eu-north-1]. 'US' or 'United States' or 'America' → [us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2]. 'Asia Pacific' or 'APAC' or 'Asia' → [ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-south-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-northeast-2]. 'UK' → [eu-west-2]. 'Australia' → [ap-southeast-2]. Multiple regions: 'US and Europe' → combine both region lists. Include home region in the list. Be inclusive - if user says 'Europe', include all European regions.
inference.validation_note: Must output array of valid AWS region codes, e.g., ["eu-west-2", "eu-central-1"]

questions.presentation_template: Based on '{{user_description}}', I'll allow these regions: {{region_list}}. This includes {{region_count}} regions for {{coverage_description}}.

questions.text: Should public S3 buckets be prevented?
questions.help_text: Recommended - blocks creation of publicly accessible S3 buckets

questions.text: Should IAM user creation be prevented outside of SSO?
questions.help_text: Recommended for centralized identity management

questions.text: Do you want to standardize tag values across your organization?
questions.help_text: AWS tag policies standardize tag key casing and restrict allowed tag values (e.g. ensuring 'Environment' is always capitalized consistently). Note: they do NOT prevent resource creation without tags — resources can still be created untagged. To block untagged resources you would need SCPs or AWS Config rules, which are not currently supported by this tool.

questions.text: Which tag keys should be standardized?
questions.help_text: Select the tag keys you want to standardize. The policy enforces consistent casing and optionally restricts allowed values — it does not block resource creation.

questions.text: Do you need automated backup policies for workload accounts?
questions.help_text: Deploys AWS Backup policies across your Workloads OU. Important: backups use tag-based selection — only resources tagged with BackupSchedule=Daily (or Weekly) will be backed up. You must tag your resources after deployment for backups to take effect. Cost: charged on backup storage used (~$0.05/GB/month for EBS snapshots, varies by service).

questions.text: What backup frequency do you need?
questions.help_text: Resources must be tagged BackupSchedule=Daily or BackupSchedule=Weekly to be included in the backup plan.

questions.text: How long should backups be retained?
questions.help_text: How long to keep backup copies

questions.text: Should default VPCs be deleted in all accounts?
questions.help_text: Recommended - removes insecure default network configurations

questions.text: How many Availability Zones should workload VPCs span?
questions.help_text: More AZs provide higher availability but increase costs

questions.text: Should workload VPCs be automatically created for accounts in the Workloads OU?
questions.help_text: Automatically provisions VPCs when new workload accounts are created

questions.text: Do you want to use AWS IPAM for centralized IP address management?
questions.help_text: IPAM (IP Address Manager) centrally manages and allocates CIDR ranges across your accounts, preventing IP conflicts. It adds some complexity and setup overhead. If disabled, VPCs use explicit CIDR allocation instead. The default IPAM pool uses 10.100.0.0/16 — if this conflicts with your existing network ranges, enable IPAM so you can configure it. Cost: free for private IP management; charges apply only if you enable public IP insights (~$0.00027/IP/hour).

questions.text: Do you want a centralized Endpoint VPC for private access to AWS services like S3 and DynamoDB? This avoids sending service traffic through NAT Gateway, reducing cost and improving security.
questions.help_text: Creates a dedicated VPC with interface endpoints shared across all workload VPCs via Transit Gateway. Reduces NAT Gateway data processing charges for AWS service traffic.

questions.text: Do you want to deploy hybrid DNS (Route 53 Resolver) to forward DNS between AWS and your on-premises network?
questions.help_text: Deploys inbound/outbound Route 53 Resolver endpoints in the Network account with a FORWARD rule to your on-prem DNS, shared org-wide. Requires a dedicated Network account. Only enable if you have on-premises DNS servers to integrate with. Cost: ~$0.125/hr per resolver endpoint ENI (two ENIs per endpoint) plus $0.40 per million queries.

questions.text: Which on-premises DNS domains should be forwarded from AWS? Enter a comma-separated list (e.g. corp.example.com, internal.example.com).
questions.help_text: DNS queries for these domains are forwarded from AWS to your on-premises DNS servers via the outbound resolver endpoint.

questions.text: What are your on-premises DNS server IP addresses? Enter a comma-separated list (e.g. 192.168.1.10, 192.168.1.11).
questions.help_text: The target DNS servers the FORWARD rule sends queries to. Must be reachable from the Network account VPC over your hybrid connection.

questions.text: Which source CIDR ranges may send DNS queries to the inbound resolver? Enter a comma-separated list (e.g. 192.168.0.0/16, 10.0.0.0/8).
questions.help_text: On-premises networks allowed to resolve AWS private DNS via the inbound resolver endpoint's security group.

questions.text: Do you want centralized internet egress via an Inspection/Egress VPC?
questions.help_text: Provides a single controlled exit point for internet traffic from all VPCs via Transit Gateway. Requires a dedicated Network account — the Inspection/Egress VPC is deployed there via StackSet. Cost: Transit Gateway ~$0.05/hr + $0.02/GB data processed; NAT Gateway in the egress VPC ~$0.045/hr per AZ plus data transfer charges.

questions.text: Do you want AWS Network Firewall in the Inspection VPC for traffic inspection?
questions.help_text: Adds deep packet inspection and stateful firewall rules - recommended for regulated environments but adds cost. Cost: ~$0.395/hr per AZ for the firewall endpoint (~$285/month for 2 AZs) plus $0.065/GB data processed.

questions.text: Do you want to enable Network Firewall logging?
questions.help_text: Logs sent to centralized S3 bucket in Log Archive account

sections.name: Logging and Monitoring
sections.description: VPC Flow Logs and log retention

questions.text: Do you want to enable the VPC Flow Logs S3 bucket in Log Archive account?
questions.help_text: Creates a centralized S3 bucket in your Log Archive account for storing VPC Flow Logs. Required if you choose S3 as the flow log destination.

questions.text: Do you want to enable VPC Flow Logs? Note: this applies to the centralized Inspection/Egress VPC only — flow logs on workload VPCs must be enabled separately after deployment.
questions.help_text: Enables VPC Flow Logs on the centralized Inspection/Egress VPC (if enabled). Note: flow logs are NOT automatically enabled on workload VPCs — you will need to enable those separately per account after deployment.

questions.text: VPC Flow Logs for the centralized Inspection/Egress VPC are delivered to the central S3 bucket in the Log Archive account. Confirm S3 as the destination.
questions.help_text: The landing zone centralizes flow logs to the Log Archive S3 bucket, which is cost-effective for long-term storage. CloudWatch Logs delivery is not offered for the centralized Inspection/Egress VPC; enable CloudWatch flow logs per workload VPC/account after deployment if you need real-time queries.

questions.text: How long should logs be retained?
questions.help_text: Longer retention useful for compliance and forensics but increases storage costs

questions.text: What is your expected monthly AWS spend (USD)?
questions.help_text: Used to set up budget alerts

questions.text: Should alerts be sent when 80% of budget is reached?
questions.help_text: Proactive notification before overspending

questions.text: What email address should receive budget alerts?
questions.help_text: Email for budget notifications

sections.name: Account Email Addresses
sections.description: Email addresses for AWS accounts. IMPORTANT: Each email must be globally unique across ALL of AWS. Plus-addressed emails (user+tag@domain.com) often collide with existing accounts. Use dedicated mailboxes or distribution lists. If account creation fails due to EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS, the failed account cannot be rolled back (AWS retains it).

questions.text: What is your organization's email domain?
questions.help_text: e.g., example.com - used for AWS account root emails

questions.text: What email address should be used for the Management account?
questions.help_text: Usually your existing AWS account email

questions.text: What email address should be used for the Log Archive account?
questions.help_text: Must be globally unique across AWS. Avoid plus-addressed emails (e.g., user+logarchive@domain.com) as they often collide. Use a dedicated mailbox or distribution list.

questions.text: What email address should be used for the Audit account?
questions.help_text: Must be globally unique across AWS. Avoid plus-addressed emails (e.g., user+audit@domain.com) as they often collide. Use a dedicated mailbox or distribution list.

questions.text: What email address should be used for the Network account?
questions.help_text: Must be globally unique across AWS. Avoid plus-addressed emails. Use a dedicated mailbox or distribution list.

questions.text: What email address should be used for the SharedServices account?
questions.help_text: Must be globally unique across AWS. Avoid plus-addressed emails. Use a dedicated mailbox or distribution list.

questions.text: What email address should be used for the Monitoring account?
questions.help_text: Must be globally unique across AWS. Avoid plus-addressed emails. Use a dedicated mailbox or distribution list.

questions.text: This starter configuration includes the options you selected above. It does NOT include: advanced security services (GuardDuty, Security Hub), CloudWatch alarms, Identity Center, or CloudTrail data events. Do you understand these limitations and want to proceed?
questions.help_text: Additional features can be added later as the generator capabilities expand
